agencies: The agencies table stores the profile of each of the four participating agencies — the Bureau of Fire Protection, the Philippine National Police, the City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office, and the City Health Office. It holds the agency code, name, location, contact details, and logo, together with the number of days before expiry at which a driver license is flagged as expiring soon. That threshold is stored here rather than fixed in the program so that each agency may set its own warning period. Each record represents one agency and serves as the reference that separates every other record in the system by agency.
users: The users table stores every account in the system, both Agency Administrators and Authorized Drivers, distinguished by the role field. Administrators and drivers are kept in one table because both must sign in, and a driver record and a login account are always the same person. The license number and license expiry date are filled in for drivers and left empty for administrators, and the device token is used to deliver push notifications to the mobile application. The status field records whether a self-registered driver is still pending approval, active, or rejected. Each record represents one person who can sign in to the system.
vehicles: The vehicles table stores the fleet of each agency, including the vehicle type, plate number, make, model, engine number, chassis number, and current odometer reading. It also carries the single shared operational status of the vehicle — Operational, Dispatched, Not Operational, or Under Preventive Maintenance — which every module reads and writes so that all screens report the same condition. The assigned driver field names the primary Authorized Driver of the vehicle. Each record represents one physical vehicle belonging to one agency.
inspection_checklist_items: The inspection checklist items table stores the standard BLOWBAGETS checklist used for daily inspections. It contains the twelve standard items — Battery, Lights, Oil, Water, Brakes, Air, Gas, Engine, Tires, Power Steering, Horn/Siren, and Directional Signals — and the two additional items that apply only to BFP vehicles, Hydraulic System and Fire Pump. This is a reference list shared by all four agencies rather than an operational record, so it is not scoped to any single agency. Each record represents one item that a driver assesses during an inspection.
inspections: The inspections table stores each daily BLOWBAGETS inspection submitted by an Authorized Driver from the mobile application. It records the vehicle inspected, the driver who performed it, the date of the inspection, and the review state, which begins as Pending and becomes Reviewed once an Agency Administrator has assessed it. When the inspection is reviewed, the administrator who reviewed it and the date and time of the review are also recorded. Each record represents one complete inspection of one vehicle on one occasion.
inspection_items: The inspection items table stores the individual results of an inspection. Each row links one inspection to one checklist item and records whether that item was found to be OK or to have an issue, together with the driver's remarks. Remarks are required whenever an item is flagged as having an issue, so that a reported fault is always explained. Each record represents the result of a single checklist item within a single inspection.
damage_reports: The damage reports table stores the standardized damage reports submitted by Authorized Drivers. It records the vehicle concerned, the driver who filed the report, a description of the nature of the damage, the parts suspected to be defective, and an optional photo attachment. The date reported is set automatically on submission, and the status begins as Pending until an Agency Administrator assesses the report and marks it Reviewed. Each record represents one reported instance of damage to one vehicle.
repair_logs: The repair logs table stores the repair activities carried out on each vehicle. It records the date of the repair, the scope of work performed, the parts replaced, the optional cost, and the source of the repair — Internal Office, GSO Motorpool, or External Repair Shop — with the name of the shop recorded when the repair was performed externally. The driver assigned to the vehicle at the time may also be recorded. Each record represents one repair activity performed on one vehicle.
pm_schedules: The preventive maintenance schedules table stores the maintenance plans set for each vehicle. A schedule is either mileage-based, using a kilometre interval and the odometer reading at the last service, or time-based, using a due date. Each schedule carries its own Due Soon threshold, set by the Agency Administrator, so that the warning period may differ from one service to another. The status moves through Upcoming, Due Soon, Due, and Completed, and the completion fields record the date serviced, the source of the service, the shop where it was performed externally, the parts replaced, and any remarks. Each record represents one maintenance cycle for one service target on one vehicle.
dispatches: The dispatches table stores the record of each vehicle deployment. It records the vehicle and driver dispatched, the mission type and location, and the date and time out, with an optional odometer reading taken as the vehicle leaves. Opening a dispatch automatically sets the vehicle status to Dispatched. When the dispatch is closed, the date and time in, an optional odometer reading on arrival, the return status of the vehicle, and any remarks are recorded; a time-in reading higher than the vehicle's current mileage updates that mileage. A dispatch with no time in is still active. Each record represents one deployment of one vehicle on one mission.
notifications: The notifications table stores the alerts raised by the system for both Authorized Drivers and Agency Administrators. It records the recipient, the category of the alert, the headline and body text, and a reference payload identifying the record the alert concerns. The read flag and the date and time read allow an Agency Administrator to keep their own notification list manageable as alerts accumulate. Each record represents one alert addressed to one user.
